Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the shopper journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it. Each dot is one automation.

  1. 1Discover3 automations
  2. 2Evaluate2 automations

1

Discover

Shoppers find products through marketplace search, Google Shopping and Meta catalog ads, creators and quick-commerce apps. Complete, consistent and honest listings decide whether a product is shown, trusted and compared fairly.

Touchpoints

  • Marketplace search and listings
  • Google Shopping and Meta catalog ads
  • Creator and influencer content
  • Quick-commerce apps

Accountable owner

Head of e-commerce or marketplace manager

Automations on this stage

  • DiscoverAI catalog enrichment with mandatory-field checksTurn supplier sheets, pack photos and spec documents into complete, channel-ready listings. AI drafts titles, attributes and descriptions from approved facts, rules check mandatory declarations, and a category owner approves every listing before it goes live.4–6 weeks
  • DiscoverStock, price and batch sync across every sales channelKeep sellable stock, prices and offers consistent across the D2C store, marketplaces and quick-commerce partners. Buffers prevent overselling, near-expiry batches are held back or proposed for markdown, and rate-linked prices such as gold jewelry are recalculated for approval.5–8 weeks
  • DiscoverCreator collaboration and ad-disclosure workflowRun creator and influencer programs from brief to repost with clear records: product seeding, approved claims sheets, disclosure checks, usage rights and sales by creator code. Built for beauty brands, where claims and disclosure draw close scrutiny.3–5 weeks
2

Evaluate

The shopper compares size, shade, specs, price and trust signals. High-value buyers want to talk to someone before they commit.

Touchpoints

  • Product page with size, shade or spec guides
  • WhatsApp and web chat questions
  • Video or showroom consultations
  • Price and offer comparison

Accountable owner

Customer experience lead or store experience manager

Automations on this stage

  • EvaluateGrounded fit, shade and spec advisorAnswer pre-purchase questions on size and fit, shade and skin type, or technical specs using only the brand's own size charts, shade guides, spec sheets and policies. When the answer is not in the approved sources, the assistant says so and hands over to a person.5–7 weeks
  • EvaluateVideo and showroom consultation bookingLet shoppers book a video call or showroom visit with a designer or jewelry consultant, pass the right product context to the consultant beforehand, and send follow-ups, quotes and approved financing information after the call.3–5 weeks
3

Checkout and confirm

The shopper pays online or chooses cash on delivery. Abandoned checkouts, unconfirmed COD orders and suspicious high-value orders are handled here, before anything ships.

Touchpoints

  • Cart and checkout
  • Payment gateway or COD choice
  • Order confirmation on WhatsApp, SMS or email
  • High-value order verification

Accountable owner

D2C growth lead with the order-operations lead

Automations on this stage

  • Checkout and confirmConsented cart and checkout recoveryFollow up abandoned carts only with shoppers who opted in, on the channel they chose, with honest messages: no fake countdowns, no pre-added items, the total price including fees shown upfront, and a clear way to opt out.2–4 weeks
  • Checkout and confirmCOD confirmation, address checks and high-value verificationConfirm cash-on-delivery orders on WhatsApp before dispatch, fix incomplete addresses, and hold risky or high-value orders for a person to review, so fewer parcels travel to doorsteps that will refuse them.3–5 weeks
4

Deliver

Parcels move through couriers, bulky items need a slot and an assembly or installation crew, and custom pieces pass through production. Each step needs clear updates and a fast fix when something slips.

Touchpoints

  • Shipping and out-for-delivery updates
  • Failed delivery attempts and reattempts
  • Delivery, installation or assembly slots
  • Made-to-order milestones

Accountable owner

Fulfillment and logistics lead

Automations on this stage

  • DeliverProactive delivery updates and failed-delivery (NDR) resolutionSend the order updates shoppers actually need and act fast when a courier reports a failed delivery attempt: confirm the reason with the shopper, capture a new slot or corrected address, and send the reattempt instruction to the courier before cut-off.3–5 weeks
  • DeliverDelivery slots, installation and warranty activationSchedule delivery, installation, demo or assembly with the shopper and the service partner, capture serial numbers and photos at the visit, and activate the warranty automatically so later service starts from a verified record.4–6 weeks
  • DeliverCustom and made-to-order progress trackingGive custom jewelry and made-to-order furniture buyers a clear timeline, from design approval through production, quality checks and hallmarking where it applies, to delivery, with proactive updates whenever a date moves.3–5 weeks
5

Returns and support

Shoppers ask questions, request returns or exchanges, report damage and open service tickets. Speed, consistency with the published policy and fair decisions protect the relationship.

Touchpoints

  • Return and exchange requests
  • Damage and defect claims
  • Order, policy and product-care questions
  • Service tickets and complaints

Accountable owner

Head of customer experience

Automations on this stage

  • Returns and supportReturns, exchanges and damage claims with photo evidenceLet shoppers start a return, size exchange or damage claim in a few taps, check eligibility against the published policy, collect photos or unboxing video where needed, and route refunds and replacements to a person when evidence or value calls for it.4–6 weeks
  • Returns and supportPolicy-grounded support assistant with human handoffAnswer order, policy, product-care and service questions on WhatsApp and web chat from the store's own policies and live order data, raise service and quality tickets with the right details, and hand over to an agent whenever a question needs judgment.5–8 weeks
6

Repeat and advocate

Consumables run out, sizes come back in stock, new collections launch and happy buyers leave reviews. A few timely, consented messages do more than constant sale blasts.

Touchpoints

  • Replenishment and subscription reminders
  • Reviews and customer photos
  • New drops and back-in-stock alerts
  • Occasion and loyalty journeys

Accountable owner

CRM and retention manager

Automations on this stage

  • Repeat and advocateReplenishment, subscription and retailer reorder remindersRemind consumers when a pack is likely to run out, run subscribe-and-save without traps, turn sample buyers into full-size customers, and let retailers and distributors reorder their usual basket on WhatsApp for a sales rep to confirm.4–6 weeks
  • Repeat and advocateReviews, drops, back-in-stock and lifecycle journeysUse RFM segments and stated preferences to send the few messages shoppers value: review and photo requests after delivery, back-in-stock and new-drop alerts they signed up for, and reminders for occasions they chose to share, with reviews published unedited.4–6 weeks

Where people stay in control

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
AI catalog enrichment with mandatory-field checksDiscoverThe category or catalog manager approves every new or changed listing. Claims about cosmetics, food or nutrition go to the client's regulatory or legal reviewer before publishing.
Stock, price and batch sync across every sales channelDiscoverThe pricing or marketplace manager approves price changes, markdown proposals and any jewelry price move beyond the tolerance. For jewelry, a named person confirms the day rate before it is used.
Creator collaboration and ad-disclosure workflowDiscoverThe brand manager approves every brief and final post. Claims about efficacy, skin conditions or ingredients go to the client's regulatory or legal reviewer; AI only flags issues.
Grounded fit, shade and spec advisorEvaluateCategory owners approve the knowledge sources and answer style before launch. Agents take over low-confidence, sensitive or out-of-scope conversations, and a reviewer samples transcripts every week.
Video and showroom consultation bookingEvaluateConsultants own every quote, custom-design commitment and price exception. Financing eligibility is decided only by the lender, never by the automation.
Consented cart and checkout recoveryCheckout and confirmThe CRM or growth manager approves templates, frequency caps, any offer and the holdout design. The client's legal or compliance owner reviews message wording against the dark-pattern guidelines before launch.
COD confirmation, address checks and high-value verificationCheckout and confirmAn order-operations reviewer decides every held or high-value order: release, call the shopper or cancel. Cancellations the shopper asks for are processed as requested; the automation never cancels an order on its own.
Proactive delivery updates and failed-delivery (NDR) resolutionDeliverThe logistics lead reviews disputed NDR reasons and courier escalations. A CX agent decides refunds or reships for perishable or delayed orders.
Delivery slots, installation and warranty activationDeliverThe service coordinator handles rescheduling conflicts, serial mismatches and damaged-on-arrival cases. Replacement and refund decisions stay with the brand's service manager.
Custom and made-to-order progress trackingDeliverThe store manager or designer agrees design changes, revised quotes and new dates with the buyer. The quality team signs off every piece before dispatch.
Returns, exchanges and damage claims with photo evidenceReturns and supportA returns agent approves every refund or replacement outside the automatic rules, every damage and defect claim, and any high-value item. Disputed claims go to the CX lead.
Policy-grounded support assistant with human handoffReturns and supportAgents own refunds, compensation, safety and quality complaints and every policy exception; the grievance officer handles escalated complaints. A QA reviewer samples conversations every week.
Replenishment, subscription and retailer reorder remindersRepeat and advocateThe CRM manager approves reminder timing and offers. For retailer orders, the sales rep or distributor confirms credit limits, schemes and the final order before dispatch.
Reviews, drops, back-in-stock and lifecycle journeysRepeat and advocateThe CRM manager approves segments, frequency caps and copy. A moderator reviews flagged reviews under a published moderation policy, guided by the voluntary BIS standard IS 19000:2022, and never removes a review for being negative.
